author: BBC News
description:
The list of some of the world's most rich and powerful people with ties to late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein has lengthened, after the US government released millions of new files from its investigation into the disgraced financier.

The latest drop of material on 30 January included three million pages, 180,000 images, 2,000 videos, and a number of household names like Richard Branson, Bill Gates and Elon Musk.

There is no suggestion that appearing in the documents implies any wrongdoing. Many people who have featured in previous releases have denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein.

Here is what we know so far and about the seismic impact they have had.

author: BBC News
description:
Delegates from the US and Iran have met for indirect talks in Oman, amid continuing fears of a military confrontation between the two countries.
 
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the talks were held in a "very positive atmosphere" and that the two countries have agreed to proceed with more negotiations.
 
He reiterated that Tehran was only prepared to discuss its nuclear programme; Washington has wanted to focus on the country's ballistic missiles and armed proxies as well. 
 
Shortly after the talks ended in Muscat, Washington announced new sanctions to curb Iran's oil exports.
 
The meeting comes as Donald Trump's 'Armada' maintains its presence in the Middle East, in response to Iran's violent repression of nationwide anti-government protests last month.

description:
The president says he’ll honour the results of the midterms "if the elections are honest”.

Subscribe here: http://bit.ly/1rbfUog

This week Donald Trump has doubled down on why he thinks power should be taken away from individual states when it comes to running elections. 

Instead, he says federal government should be running elections - contrary to the U.S. constitution - claiming there is too much corruption from “crooked” blue Democrat states.

In this episode, Justin and Anthony unpack what the president is proposing, and look at other ways Republicans could disrupt this year’s midterms. Also, is there a way Trump may be able to effectively cancel or stop the midterms from happening at all?

And we hear another entry into the ‘United States of Americast’ - this time from Jenny in Utah who tells us about the issues that matter in the ‘Beehive State’.

description:
A high-profile general in Russia's military has been shot several times and wounded in Moscow.

Lt Gen Vladimir Alexeyev was immediately taken to hospital after the attack in a residential block of flats on the north-western outskirts of the Russian capital and his condition is unknown.

Alexeyev is number two in the main directorate of Russia's GRU military intelligence and the latest high-ranking military figure to have been targeted in the capital since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began almost four years ago.

It is not yet known who was behind the shooting on Friday morning.

If you check into a hotel room in China you may not be as alone as you think.
 
Criminals are hiding cameras in hotels across the country to secretly film and even livestream unsuspecting guests having sex.
 
So-called spy-cam porn is then sold online for strangers to watch. For victims the impact can be devastating.
 
Now a BBC Eye investigation has uncovered evidence about one of the networks running this illegal trade.

At least 31 people have been killed in an explosion at a Shia mosque during Friday prayers in the Pakistani capital Islamabad, officials have said.

The blast at the mosque in the Tarlai area of the city prompted an emergency to be declared at three hospitals in the city.

The cause of the blast was not immediately clear, however reports suggest it was carried out by a suicide bomber.

Pakistan's president said "targeting innocent civilians is a crime against humanity".

author: BBC News
description:
Senior US and Iranian officials are expected to meet in Oman for direct talks in the coming hours, amid a crisis that has raised fears of a military confrontation between the two countries.
 
The discussions come after a US military build-up in the Middle East in response to Iran's violent repression of nationwide anti-government protests last month, that human rights groups say killed many thousands of people.
 
Uncertainty over the location and scope had threatened to derail the talks, which are part of a diplomatic effort by regional mediators to de-escalate tensions.
 
Both countries remain far apart in their positions. The hope is that, if successful, the discussions could lead to a framework for negotiations.
